skills.title: Staying Safe at Home and Outside
skills.description: Pick safe choices at home, like having a fire escape plan, washing hands, and being careful with the phone and door. Also pick safe choices outside, like wearing sunscreen, riding the bus safely, and being careful around animals and train tracks.

skills.title: Food Allergies and Reactions
skills.description: Some people have allergies to foods like peanuts, milk, eggs, or fish. Match common food allergies to the reactions they can cause.

skills.title: Medicines and Using Them Safely
skills.description: Some medicines need a doctor's prescription and some do not. Sort examples of each and pick the safe rules for using medicine.

skills.title: Hard Times in Body and Brain
skills.description: When things feel hard, your body and brain can feel tired, hot, overwhelmed, or ready to cry. Match these feelings to things that can help you feel better.

skills.title: Healthy Choices with the Food Guide
skills.description: Use Canada's Food Guide to pick foods and drinks that help you eat well. Choose healthy meals and snacks, even when you can't pick everything.

skills.title: Consent and Standing Up
skills.description: You get to say no to things that make you uncomfortable, and others do too. Pick ways to state your limits, respect other people's no, and tell a trusted adult about improper touching.

skills.title: Naming Feelings to Get Help
skills.description: Words like calm, sad, angry, scared, and worried name feelings. Match feelings to times when you might need to ask for help.

skills.title: Getting Along and Hurtful Actions
skills.description: Cooperating, showing respect, and listening help you get along with others. Tell these from hurtful actions like name calling, ignoring, and hitting.

skills.title: Healing Without Medicine
skills.description: Sleep, fresh air, exercise, and healthy food can help your body feel better. Match these healthy habits to the problems they can help with.
